critical_analysis.question: For applicant app_000g, estimate over a 10-year horizon the likelihood of completion, volunteering, cheerleading, donating, and recruiting for the LEAD Certificate alumni community, using only consented application and interaction data plus cohort base rates.
hypotheses: H1: The applicant will be a high-fit long-term community member. Evidence for: upward term scores, 32 months of volunteer coordination, 21 months of mentoring, 1 referral made, and interview notes describing energy and alumni-network interest. Evidence against: standard hardest course load, 0 campus visits, and moderate response time. Evidence quality: mostly direct for activities and interaction data, anecdotal for interview and statement.

H2: The applicant is primarily career-ambitious and may complete but remain only moderately engaged with the institution. Evidence for: stated goal to run a fund, standard course load, 0 campus visits, and only 2 events attended. Evidence against: volunteering, mentoring, crediting colleagues, and an existing referral. Evidence quality: direct for interaction/activity fields, indirect for interpreting motives from goals.
critical_analysis.base_rate_used: Used LEAD Certificate alumni reference-class base rates before estimating: completion 0.62, volunteer 0.31, cheerleader 0.28, donor 0.14, recruiter 0.22. Applicant-specific signals were treated as adjustments from these base rates, not as causal proof.
inconsistencies: No instruction-injection or request to ignore evaluation rules appeared in the applicant text.

No major inconsistency found across statement, activities, academic trajectory, institution interactions, and interview notes: the mentoring, reciprocity, and network-interest signals are mutually reinforcing.
Potential overclaim risk: the statement reports recovering 80% of churned accounts, but this is self-reported and not independently verified.
circumstance_signals_excluded: No current wealth or family resources used for donor prediction.
No school prestige, location, family background, or other circumstance signal used as evidence.
Program reference class was used only as a cohort base rate, not as an individual circumstance advantage.
critical_analysis.strongest_case_for: The applicant combines a better-than-base completion profile with repeated reciprocity behaviors: improving term scores, persistence after setbacks, 32 months of volunteer coordination, 21 months of mentoring, continued mentoring, crediting colleagues, alumni-network interest, and 1 observed referral.
critical_analysis.strongest_case_against: The institutional-affinity evidence is still shallow: 0 campus visits, only 2 events attended, 2 questions asked, and no direct history of giving or sustained alumni-service behavior. Some of the strongest performance claims are self-reported.
what_would_change_my_mind: Completion estimate would decrease if instructor references or later term results showed declining performance, missed deadlines, or inability to manage workload.
Volunteer and recruiter estimates would decrease if the applicant declined a low-friction volunteer or ambassador opportunity without a practical constraint.
Cheerleader estimate would decrease if post-admission interactions showed low responsiveness or negative sentiment toward the institution.
Donor estimate would decrease if later evidence showed low gratitude toward the institution, no sustained reciprocity, or career trajectory inconsistent with the stated ambition.
Estimates would increase if the applicant completed a demanding pre-work module early, recruited another qualified candidate, or volunteered for an alumni/community event.
critical_analysis.proposed_experiment: Cheapest falsification tests: for completion, assign an optional rigorous pre-work module with a short deadline; for volunteer, invite the applicant to a one-hour service or mentoring event; for cheerleader, ask for a short reflection on why they would recommend the program; for donor, track non-monetary reciprocity such as mentoring and referrals before considering giving; for recruiter, offer a low-effort ambassador referral task and observe follow-through.
critical_analysis.analogy_and_where_it_breaks: The main analogy is to prior LEAD Certificate alumni base rates. It is useful because applicants share the same program context and alumni opportunity set. It breaks because this applicant has unusually strong direct mentoring and volunteer history plus an early referral, while also having only moderate institution-specific engagement so far. Correlation is not causation: volunteering and referrals correlate with future engagement but do not prove the program will cause it.
